question: Looking at Belfius' consolidated credit risk exposure (Bank and Insurer combined, measured as Full Exposure at Default, FEAD) by counterparty type, which of the main counterparty categories (central governments, public sector entities, corporate, project finance, retail, financial institutions, other) recorded the largest increase in FEAD between 31 December 2024 and 31 December 2025, and by how much in EUR million?
reference_answer: Retail recorded the largest increase: FEAD rose from EUR 64,916 million at 31 December 2024 to EUR 68,279 million at 31 December 2025, i.e. +EUR 3,363 million. For comparison, the other categories changed by: corporate +EUR 2,178 million (55,686 to 57,864), financial institutions +EUR 1,328 million (13,413 to 14,741), central governments +EUR 302 million (34,336 to 34,638), project finance -EUR 273 million (2,397 to 2,124), other -EUR 1,107 million (4,551 to 3,444) and public sector entities -EUR 1,198 million (41,286 to 40,088). Total FEAD was EUR 221,178 million (2024: EUR 216,585 million).

question: In Luzerner Kantonalbank's 2025 disclosure report, which market risk category (general interest rate, equity, commodity, foreign exchange, credit spread, default risk or residual risk add-on) required the most regulatory capital under the standardised approach at 31 December 2025, and how much in CHF million?
reference_answer: Credit spread risk (non-securitisations) required the most capital: CHF 140.7 million at 31 December 2025, out of a total market risk capital requirement of CHF 335.0 million. The other categories were equity risk CHF 75.4 million, foreign exchange risk CHF 44.0 million, general interest rate risk CHF 32.9 million, default risk (non-securitisations) CHF 29.3 million, commodity risk CHF 8.1 million and residual risk add-on CHF 4.5 million.

question: Rank the three asset classes with the largest risk-weighted assets (RWA) under Luzerner Kantonalbank's standardised approach for credit risk at 31 December 2025, considering the main asset classes only (not the 'of which' sub-lines), and give the RWA of each in CHF million.
reference_answer: 1) Directly and indirectly secured real estate exposures: CHF 19,055.2 million; 2) Corporates: CHF 2,949.3 million; 3) Retail: CHF 530.2 million. The next largest is public-sector entities at CHF 410.9 million. Total RWA under the standardised approach is CHF 24,113.5 million.

question: Did ASN Bank's total capital ratio at 31 December 2025 exceed its overall capital requirement (OCR) as shown in its Pillar 3 key metrics? Give both figures.
reference_answer: Yes. ASN Bank's total capital ratio was 24.13% at 31 December 2025, above its overall capital requirement of 16.16% (total SREP own funds requirement of 11.50% plus combined buffer requirement of 4.66%), a headroom of 7.97 percentage points.

question: Compare the leverage ratio of ASN Bank at 31 December 2025 with that of Commonwealth Bank of Australia (Europe) N.V. at 30 June 2025, both as reported in their Pillar 3 key metrics. Which was higher and by how many percentage points?
reference_answer: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (Europe) N.V. had the higher leverage ratio: 20.79% at 30 June 2025, versus 5.09% for ASN Bank at 31 December 2025, a gap of 15.70 percentage points.

question: In how many of the six supervisory interest rate shock scenarios did Luzerner Kantonalbank's economic value of equity (EVE) decrease at 31 December 2025, and which scenarios were they?
reference_answer: EVE decreased in 3 of the 6 scenarios at 31 December 2025: parallel down (CHF -285.4 million), flattener (CHF -241.5 million) and short rate up (CHF -123.9 million). It increased under parallel up (+CHF 120.5 million), steepener (+CHF 247.9 million) and short rate down (+CHF 130.7 million).

question: How did ASN Bank's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital evolve at the five quarter-end reporting dates from 31 December 2024 to 31 December 2025, in € million?
reference_answer: CET1 capital was €3,442 million at 31 December 2024 (CRR 2 basis), €3,587 million at 31 March 2025, €3,586 million at 30 June 2025, €3,626 million at 30 September 2025 and €3,613 million at 31 December 2025 (CRR 3 basis from March 2025). Overall it rose by €171 million over the year, peaking at the end of September 2025, with small dips at 30 June and 31 December 2025.

question: What reasons does Commonwealth Bank of Australia (Europe) N.V. give in its Pillar 3 report for the movement in its standardised-approach credit risk and counterparty credit risk risk exposure amounts between 30 June 2024 and 30 June 2025?
reference_answer: For standardised-approach credit risk, the bank says the amount remained relatively stable versus FY2024 (EUR 1,045,267 thousand at 30 June 2025 versus EUR 1,057,993 thousand at 30 June 2024); the small decrease is attributed to less exposure to institutions. For counterparty credit risk (CCR), TREA increased (EUR 15,867 thousand versus EUR 8,704 thousand) because the bank entered 6 new derivatives transactions, which increased the potential future exposure on interest rate derivatives and thereby the exposure value.

question: ASN Bank's credit risk exposure amount at 31 December 2025 includes an Article 3 CRR add-on of € 1,879 million for pending IRB model refinements on non-NHG mortgages. Purely as a mechanical recomputation, what would ASN Bank's CET1 ratio be at 31 December 2025 if that add-on were removed from the total risk exposure amount and CET1 capital stayed unchanged? Round to two decimals.
reference_answer: About 22.06%. Removing the €1,879 million add-on from the total risk exposure amount of €18,259 million gives €16,380 million; CET1 capital of €3,613 million divided by €16,380 million is 22.06%, versus the reported 19.79% (a purely mechanical figure that ignores any other effect of removing the add-on).

evidence.text: in € millions1 … 2. This includes an Article 3 CRR add-on of € 1,879 million pending further refinements to be made in IRB modelling regarding non-NHG mortgages.

question: Does Belfius Bank's Prudential Transition Plan set a quantitative limit on ESG-related credit risk exposure, and if so what is the limit?
reference_answer: This cannot be established from the available documents. Belfius' 2025 risk report only states that the Prudential Transition Plan is a regulatory document giving an overview of the strategic actions and risk management tools Belfius deploys for ESG risks, and that it is not disclosed publicly (it is assessed by the supervisor as part of the SREP); no limits or quantitative targets from the plan are reported in any of the 12 documents.
